meta.storyTitle: Show a human-readable timestamp in the dev-chat who-row (user left, provider right, smaller font)
meta.triageRationale: One cohesive UX add: an optional ts on the transcript row, rendered as a smaller, opposite-end-aligned time in the existing who-row. It touches a small, known set of files inside the single chat module (render-registry.ts host mirror + webview string + CSS, session-store.ts TranscriptEntry, the row-creation sites in chat-panel/turn-lifecycle/session-file-store, and the parity tests), with one obvious approach (optional field, default-now, render in whoRow) and no new contract or storage-schema change — a session-file-store row simply gains an optional field. That is a small (one story, few tasks), not trivial: it spans more than one file and needs the host/webview parity kept. [LLD note: the rationale above was written at triage time and sketches the a2-shaped 'optional ts field' idea; the LLD body's chosenAlternative is a1 — reuse the existing persisted `at`, no new TranscriptEntry/session-store field — which a2 was explicitly rejected for duplicating. The triage text is kept verbatim for provenance; the body is authoritative.]

alternativesConsidered.name: Render existing `at` in the who-row (smallest, no data change)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Format the already-persisted `at` ISO field in whoRow as a small muted span at the opposite end of the label; zero changes to TranscriptEntry, creation sites, or persistence.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Reuse the existing `at: string` (ISO) on every TranscriptEntry (session-store.ts:31-103). Host toViewModel (render-registry.ts:116-194) passes `at` through on user/assistant RowViewModel meta; the webview whoRow (render-registry.ts:407-409, called from msgRow :404-439) takes an optional `at` and renders a `<span class='insrc-when'>` formatted with `new Date(at).toLocaleTimeString()`. Opposite-end placement: the user message row is right-aligned (insrc-msg--user, detected by transcript-pager.ts:79), so the time span is PREPENDED (left end); the assistant row is left-aligned, so the span is APPENDED with margin-left:auto (right end). New CSS `.insrc-when{font-size:10px;opacity:.65;margin:0 6px;align-self:center;}` beside `.insrc-who` (11px). Missing/invalid `at` renders no span.
pros: No protocol or persisted-data change at all — `at` exists on every row already and is set at creation (chat-panel.ts:2889, :3178).
Smallest diff: host toViewModel meta + webview whoRow + one CSS rule + parity tests; old sessions render real historical times.
Old session files need no backfill; rows with unparseable `at` degrade to today's markup.
cons: toLocaleTimeString output varies by OS locale (acceptable for a chat timestamp); formatting runs in both the host mirror and the webview string, so the parity test must pin both paths.
Parity surface grows by one field on two renderers (host meta + webview string).

alternativesConsidered.name: New optional `ts` field on the row
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add `ts?: number` to TranscriptEntry + RowViewModel and render it in whoRow, defaulting to `at` when absent.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add an optional `ts?: number` (epoch ms) to the user/assistant TranscriptEntry variant and to RowViewModel, populated with Date.now() at the same creation sites that set `at`; whoRow renders from `ts` when present, falling back to parsing `at`. This adds a second timestamp field purely for rendering convenience.
pros: Epoch ms is cheap to format in both host and webview.
Matches the request's literal suggestion of an optional ts field on the row.
cons: Duplicates `at` — two sources of truth for one fact, must be kept in sync at every creation site (chat-panel.ts:2889, :3178, plus markers/diffs).
Touches session-store.ts type, creation sites, session-file-store load path, and both renderers — strictly more surface than a1 for zero user-visible gain.
Optional field on a persisted row still needs a load-path decision for old files (default undefined).
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets the visible requirement but duplicates `at` as `ts`, adding type + creation-site + load-path surface for zero user-visible gain; only partially satisfies the no-protocol/storage-change, parity, and old-session constraints (s3 rank 2).

alternativesConsidered.name: Tooltip-only timestamp on the who-label
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Put the formatted time in the label span's title attribute; nothing new is drawn.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Render the timestamp as a `title` tooltip on the existing who-label span (render-registry.ts:407-409): set `title = new Date(at).toLocaleString()`; no new DOM node, no CSS.
cons: Not visible without hover — does not meet the requirement to SHOW the time in the who-row.
No opposite-end placement and no smaller font element at all.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Cheapest (XS) but violates the core requirement — hover-only tooltip, the time is not shown in the who-row; also no opposite-end placement and no smaller-font element (s3 rank 4).

alternativesConsidered.name: Pre-format `when` in host toViewModel, webview prints it
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Host formats `at` into a short `when` string in RowViewModel.meta; whoRow renders that string as the small opposite-end span.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Format once in the host: toViewModel emits a pre-formatted `when: string` (HH:MM via a fixed Intl.DateTimeFormat) in RowViewModel.meta; the webview whoRow prints `meta.when` verbatim and never calls Date/toLocale itself.
pros: Single formatting implementation, single place to test the string.
Webview renderer stays dumb (no Date calls in the injected string), which suits the strict-CSP fake-DOM tests.
cons: Host owns the locale/format choice; the parity test must pin the exact formatted string, slightly more test code than passing `at` raw.
Webview locale adjustment is lost (irrelevant in practice — the webview shares the host locale).
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Ties a1 behaviorally on every acceptance axis but loses on diff size: formatter plus string-pinning test live in the host mirror, while a1 passes the raw ISO `at` through the view-model and keeps row data untouched end to end (s3 rank 2).

errorCases.detection: In whoRow, `at` is parsed with `new Date(at)` and validated: the result must be a finite number (isNaN(d.getTime()) check) AND within a sane window — not in the future beyond a small clock-skew allowance (e.g. d.getTime() <= Date.now() + 60_000). An absent, unparseable, or far-future `at` yields null and no span is created.
errorCases.response: Render no .insrc-when span; the who-row falls back to the exact pre-story markup. No throw — the renderer's existing try/catch fallback still applies on top.
errorCases.scenario: A row with missing, invalid, or far-future `at` reaches the webview whoRow (old session file, hand-edited store, clock skew)
errorCases.userImpact: No timestamp on that one row; everything else renders normally.

migration.backwardCompat: Full. The change is render-only: no TranscriptEntry field is added, removed, or reformatted (the live user-row post's extra `at` field is a transient webview message, not persisted storage), so session files written by older versions load unchanged and simply render their stored `at` time, and a build without this change renders rows as before because nothing new is persisted. Rows with a missing/unparseable/far-future `at` render the old markup (no span), so hand-edited or skewed stores degrade gracefully. Rollback is reverting the single renderer commit; nothing is rewritten.

migrationSteps.action: No data migration: every persisted TranscriptEntry already has `at` (set at creation; s1 bundle c1 — session-store.ts:31-103, chat-panel.ts:2889/:3178), so no backfill of session files is needed. Renderers degrade to the old markup for any row whose `at` is missing/unparseable.

Ship the renderer + live-path change as one commit: BOTH toViewModel mirrors gain meta.at (host render-registry.ts:116-194 incl. delta branch :155-157; webview inline :464-490 incl. :480), the user-row post carries at (chat-panel.ts:2898-2905) and its webview consume passes it (chat-panel.ts:2677), whoRow gains the at? param and span.insrc-when (render-registry.ts:406-411, call site :419), and the .insrc-when rule goes into RENDER_REGISTRY_STYLE (render-registry.ts:202-315, injected at chat-panel.ts:2368). The edit set spans both mirrors + the live posting sites + one CSS rule. Rollback = revert that commit; old rows keep their `at` and nothing is rewritten.

uxDefinition.narrative: Shows the changed who-row as a SINGLE line per role (no two-line widget): the label keeps its current end of the line and the small muted time sits at the OPPOSITE end of the same line. Each who-row is a horizontal ColumnSet — the user row is right-aligned so the time sits in the LEFT column opposite the label; the assistant row is left-aligned so the time sits in the RIGHT column (margin-left:auto) opposite the label. The timestamp TextBlock is size:'small' + isSubtle:true, visibly smaller and dimmer than the bolder label, and its text uses the '<3-letter weekday>, dd/MM HH:mm' format (e.g. 'Wed, 11/11 04:18').
